_capture_meta.note: rhs_account_number omitted, so pricing reflects the caller's own user-level routing (per the tool's guide: market-maker routing if the caller has no crypto account). routing field in each result shows 'Exchange Routing' was actually applied.

raw_response.guide: Current price: prefer mark_price when both sides of the book are populated; if mark_price is zero, fall back to the most recent of bid_time / ask_time and quote the side that updated last. Drop bid or ask when zero — the book is unavailable on that side. Use updated_at to judge freshness; if it is more than a few seconds stale, phrase as "as of <time>" rather than "current". open_price is the previous close — in continuous crypto the midnight boundary price is the prior day's close. That boundary is midnight in the request timezone (the 'timezone' parameter), or US Eastern when none is supplied; response timestamps carry that same timezone's offset, so quote "as of" times in it directly. For change vs the previous close, compute (mark_price - open_price) / open_price. The response symbol comes back unhyphenated (e.g. 'BTCUSD'); the canonical form from get_currency_pairs is hyphenated ('BTC-USD') — strip the hyphen to cross-reference. bid/ask/mark reflect the execution routing reported in routing: the supplied account's routing when rhs_account_number was given, otherwise the caller's user-level routing (market maker routing when the caller has no crypto account). This is informational; place_order routing is selected per account at order time.
